I have been farming this land for fifty years. I know Quzhou's soils — the sandy loam near the well, the heavier patches on the east side. My wheat-maize rotation runs on eight of my twelve mu. The other four mu I keep in cotton — it brings in cash and I have always grown it. My husband passed three years ago so it is just my son and me now, and he works in the city most of the year. I cannot take on anything new or risky. I stick to what I know.

For wheat, I plough in October after the last cotton pick, broadcast my compound fertilizer, then sow. I use the improved variety the village seed shop sells — not the old ones my mother used, those yield too low. I irrigate three times: once before freeze, once at jointing, once at heading. Two pesticide sprays — one for rust, one for aphid in spring. Yield around 450 jin per mu is what I expect.

Right after wheat harvest in June I rotary-till and get the summer maize in fast — you cannot waste days in Hebei summer. I use hybrid seed,郑单958 or similar, whatever the supply cooperative has. Two irrigations if rain is poor. Maize does not need as much spraying.

Cotton is my hardest work. I start seedlings in late April, transplant in May on the four mu. Cotton needs potassium, more than the other crops. Bollworm is always the worry — I spray five times through the season. Four irrigations from the well. My back hurts more than it used to but I manage.
